Let $(M,g,N_0)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], and let
$\nabla$ be its unique torsion-free $g$-compatible connection supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Fix a nonempty
connected open set $O\subseteq M$. A **selected stationary thermal carrier** on
$O$ consists of a smooth future timelike vector field $\xi$ and a smooth
positive scalar field $T:O\to(0,\infty)$, where $T$ is measured in kelvins,
such that $\xi$ is a Killing field of $g$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-killing-field]]. Equivalently, the criterion is
$\nabla_{(a}\xi_{b)}=0$ by
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]]. The round brackets mean
symmetrization with factor $1/2$. The choice of $\xi$ specifies the thermal congruence; no
coordinate chart or universal observer field is selected.

Set $N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ and $u:=\xi/N_\xi$. Then
$g(u,u)=-1$. In the length-coordinate convention $x^0=ct$, $u$ is
dimensionless and $cu$ is the physical four-velocity, with $c>0$ in
$\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. For a fixed Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in
$\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, define the inverse-temperature vector
$\beta:=u/(k_BT)$, with units $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, and the Killing-normalized
temperature field $T_K:=N_\xi T$. Thus $\beta=\xi/(k_BT_K)$; this definition
does not assert that $T_K$ is constant.

For a smooth chemical-potential scalar $\mu:O\to\mathbb R$ in joules, put
$\zeta:=\mu/(k_BT)$, a dimensionless scalar. Define the rest-space metric,
derivative, acceleration, expansion and shear by
$$h_{ab}:=g_{ab}+u_au_b,\qquad D:=u^a\nabla_a,\qquad a_b:=u^a\nabla_au_b,\qquad \theta:=\nabla_au^a,\qquad \sigma_{ab}:=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)}-\frac13\theta h_{ab}.$$
Here $a$, $\theta$ and $\sigma$ have inverse-length units; the physical
proper acceleration is $c^2a$. The smooth tangent-bundle structure used by
the cited GR suppliers assumes the Axiom of Countable Choice
[[def-countable-choice]]; no stronger choice principle is part of this
definition.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ ([[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
([[def-derivative]]). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

$$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

Equivalently, since $b - a \ne 0$, there is $c \in (a,b)$ at which
$f'(c) = \bigl(f(b)-f(a)\bigr)/(b-a)$: the derivative somewhere inside equals
the average rate of change across the whole interval.

**Continuity on the closed interval cannot be dropped.** Differentiability at
every point of $(a,b)$ alone does not suffice: a function on $[0,1]$,
differentiable at every point of $(0,1)$ with derivative constantly $1$, for
which no $c$ works, is exhibited later on this page as a false statement, and
the companion page works the same witness out in full.

Differentiating $\beta=u/(k_BT)$ then gives

back gives $\sigma_{ab}=0$.

([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\xi$ be a smooth vector field
on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **Lie
derivative of the metric along $\xi$**, written $\mathcal L_\xi g$, is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field obtained by the flow definition of
[[def-lie-derivative-of-a-tensor-field]] applied to $g$: for the local flow

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0,$$

where $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],

a property of that metric: neither existence nor uniqueness of a Killing field
is asserted here, and a general metric has none beyond the trivial field

If $X$ has local flow $\Phi_t$ and $T$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(r,s)$, its Lie derivative is $$\mathcal L_XT=\left.\frac d{dt}\right|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*T,$$ on every local flow domain where this derivative is defined. Here the pullback by the local diffeomorphism $\Phi_t$ acts by $d\Phi_{-t}$ on each contravariant slot and by $d\Phi_t$ on each covariant slot.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. Tensoriality of $R$ is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a).
Lowering its output slot with the smooth metric and contracting with the
smooth inverse metric are intrinsic tensor operations
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] clauses (b)-(c),
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]]). Thus these formulas give smooth
fields of types $(0,4)$, $(0,2)$, $(0,0)$ and $(0,2)$, respectively,
independent of the chart. Symmetry of $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $G$ is proved
separately in [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clause (d).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let $R$ be
the curvature operator of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
with components $R^a{}_{bcd}$ in a chart.

**(a) Tensoriality.** For all smooth functions $f$ on $M$ and smooth vector
fields $X,Y,Z$ on a common domain, $R(X,Y)Z=-R(Y,X)Z$ and
$$R(fX,Y)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,fY)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,Y)(fZ)=fR(X,Y)Z .$$
Consequently, for every $p\in M$, the value $R(X,Y)Z|_p$ depends only on
$X_p,Y_p,Z_p$, and $R$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(1,3)$ on $M$ whose
components in every smooth chart are the functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] clause (b).

**(b) Coordinate formula.** In every smooth chart $(U,x)$ with Christoffel
symbols $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of $\nabla$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]),
$$R^a{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma^a{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^a{}_{cb} +\sum_e\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{ce}\Gamma^e{}_{db}-\Gamma^a{}_{de}\Gamma^e{}_{cb}\bigr)$$
on $U$, for all $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.

**(c) Point-normal formula.** If the chart is point-normal at $p$, that is
$g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}$, $\partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0$ and $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0$
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]), then, writing
$g_{ad,bc}:=\partial_b\partial_cg_{ad}$,
$$R_{abcd}(p)=\tfrac12\bigl(g_{ad,bc}+g_{bc,ad}-g_{bd,ac}-g_{ac,bd}\bigr)(p) .$$
Equivalently, $R^a{}_{bcd}(p)=\tfrac12\,g^{ae}(p)\bigl(\partial_b\partial_cg_{ed}
+\partial_e\partial_dg_{bc}-\partial_e\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_b\partial_dg_{ec}\bigr)(p)$.

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ ([[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
([[def-derivative]]). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

$$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

Equivalently, since $b - a \ne 0$, there is $c \in (a,b)$ at which
$f'(c) = \bigl(f(b)-f(a)\bigr)/(b-a)$: the derivative somewhere inside equals
the average rate of change across the whole interval.

**Continuity on the closed interval cannot be dropped.** Differentiability at
every point of $(a,b)$ alone does not suffice: a function on $[0,1]$,
differentiable at every point of $(0,1)$ with derivative constantly $1$, for
which no $c$ works, is exhibited later on this page as a false statement, and
the companion page works the same witness out in full.

Let $\eta$ be a Lorentz form on a $4$-dimensional real vector space $V$. There
is an ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $V$ with
$\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ for all $a,b$. Such a basis
is called **$\eta$-orthonormal**; in every $\eta$-orthonormal ordered basis
exactly one basis vector is timelike and the other three are spacelike, and the
count is the inertia $(3,1,0)$ of $\eta$.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), with causal terminology as in
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], and let

$$T:=\{v\in V:\eta(v,v)<0\}$$

be its **timelike set**. Components and closures refer to the topology obtained
by using any ordered basis to identify $V$ with Euclidean $\mathbb R^4$;
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], step 5.1, proves that the
resulting open sets are independent of the basis. By that lemma the
set $T$ has exactly two connected components, and each of them is nonempty,
open, convex and path-connected. A **time orientation** of $(V,\eta)$ is a
choice of one of these two components. Fixing such a choice, write $C^+$ for the
chosen component and

$$C^-:=T\setminus C^+$$

for the other component; thus $T=C^+\sqcup C^-$ is a disjoint union and
$C^+$, $C^-$ are exactly the two components supplied by the lemma. Relative to
this choice a vector $v\in V$ is

- **future timelike** when $v\in C^+$;
- **past timelike** when $v\in C^-$;
- **future null** when $v\neq 0$, $\eta(v,v)=0$ and $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C^+)$;
- **past null** when $v\neq 0$, $\eta(v,v)=0$ and $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C^-)$;
- **future causal** when it is future timelike or future null;
- **past causal** when it is past timelike or past null.

The sets $\operatorname{cl}(C^+)$ and $\operatorname{cl}(C^-)$ are the
**future closed cone** and the **past closed cone** of the time-oriented space
$(V,\eta,C^+)$. By [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] each of them
is a convex cone, their intersection is $\{0\}$, and a vector is causal exactly
when it is future causal or past causal, in which case exactly one of these two
alternatives holds: no nonzero vector is both future causal and past causal.
The timelike vectors are exactly the points of $T=C^+\cup C^-$, and
$0\notin T$ because $\eta(0,0)=0$; since a null vector is nonzero with
$\eta(v,v)=0$, no vector is both timelike and null, so the classes above are
mutually exclusive where the definitions say they are: no vector is both future
and past causal, and no timelike vector is null.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and let
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an $\eta$-orthonormal ordered basis. Write
$v=v^0e_0+v^1e_1+v^2e_2+v^3e_3$ for the coordinates of $v$
([[thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis]]) and

$$\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert:=\sqrt{(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2}.$$

Then $\eta(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert^2$, and the timelike set
$T:=\{v\in V:\eta(v,v)<0\}$ satisfies

$$T=T_+\cup T_-,\qquad T_+:=\{v:v^0>\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\},\qquad T_-:=\{v:v^0<-\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\}.$$

The sets $T_+$ and $T_-$ are nonempty, disjoint, open in $V$ (for the metric
topology of the distance $d(u,w):=\lVert c(u)-c(w)\rVert_2$ induced by the
coordinates $c(v):=(v^0,v^1,v^2,v^3)$), convex and path-connected, and they are
exactly the two connected components of $T$. In every $\eta$-orthonormal
ordered basis the two displayed coordinate sets coincide with the two
components of $T$ in some order, and they may be interchanged relative to a
previously fixed naming of the components. Moreover

$$\operatorname{cl}(T_+)=\{v:v^0\ge\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(T_-)=\{v:v^0\le-\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(T_+)\cap\operatorname{cl}(T_-)=\{0\}.$$

Let $V$ be a $4$-dimensional real vector space ([[def-vector-space]],
[[def-dimension]]). A **Lorentz form** on $V$ is a symmetric bilinear form
$\eta:V\times V\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-bilinear-symmetric-skew-and-alternating-forms]])
such that

1. $\eta$ is nondegenerate: both radicals
   $\operatorname{rad}_L(\eta)=\{u:\eta(u,v)=0\text{ for every }v\}$ and
   $\operatorname{rad}_R(\eta)=\{v:\eta(u,v)=0\text{ for every }u\}$ are
   $\{0\}$ ([[def-matrix-radicals-rank-and-nondegeneracy-of-a-bilinear-form]]);
   and
2. $\eta$ has **inertia** $(3,1,0)$: in some (equivalently, in every) basis of
   $V$ in which the matrix of $\eta$ is diagonal, exactly three diagonal
   entries are positive, exactly one is negative, and none is zero
   ([[def-definiteness-inertia-and-signature-data-over-the-reals]]).

The inertia of a symmetric bilinear form is the triple $(p,q,r)$ of numbers of
positive, negative and zero diagonal entries of any diagonalizing basis, and it
is independent of the diagonalizing basis by Sylvester's law of inertia
([[def-definiteness-inertia-and-signature-data-over-the-reals]]); hence clause 2
is a property of $\eta$ itself and not of a chosen basis. The **associated
quadratic form** of $\eta$ is

$$q(v):=\eta(v,v),\qquad v\in V .$$

A **Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$** is a pair $(V,\eta)$
consisting of a $4$-dimensional real vector space $V$ and a Lorentz form $\eta$
on $V$; the name records that the diagonal normal form of $\eta$ has one
negative entry followed by three positive entries. No positive-definite
structure on $V$ is assumed or implied by this definition, and $q$ takes both
negative and positive values on nonzero vectors: a basis in which
$\eta$ is diagonal with diagonal entries $-1,1,1,1$ exists by clause 2, and on
its first vector $q$ is $-1$, while on each of the other three it is $+1$.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), with associated quadratic form
$q(v)=\eta(v,v)$. A vector $v\in V$ is

- **timelike** when $q(v)<0$;
- **null**, or **lightlike**, when $v\neq 0$ and $q(v)=0$;
- **spacelike** when $q(v)>0$;
- **causal** when it is timelike or null.

The zero vector $0\in V$ satisfies $q(0)=0$ and is consequently **none** of
timelike, null or spacelike: the null case explicitly excludes it, and the
timelike and spacelike cases exclude it by $q(0)=0$ together with the strict
inequalities. The **causal character** of a nonzero vector $v$ is the sign of
the real number $q(v)$, and the three names are attached to the three signs as
above. When no confusion arises, the pairing $\eta$ itself is written
$\langle v,w\rangle:=\eta(v,w)$.

**Each nonzero vector has exactly one causal character.** For a nonzero
$v\in V$ the real number $q(v)$ satisfies exactly one of $q(v)<0$, $q(v)=0$,
$q(v)>0$ by trichotomy of the order on $\mathbb R$, so $v$ is timelike, null or
spacelike, and no two of the three alternatives can hold at once. The causal
vectors are therefore exactly the nonzero vectors that are timelike or null,
and the zero vector is causal in no sense introduced here.

In the future massive shell write $P=(E,rn)$, where
$E=\sqrt{M^2+r^2}$, $r>0$ and $n\in S^2$. Apply the assumed identity to
the two shell vectors $(E,rn)$ and $(E,-rn)$ and subtract. Dividing the
result by $2r>0$ gives
$2E A_{0i}n_i+b_i n_i=0$ for every $E>M$ and every unit $n$. For fixed $n$,
the left side is affine in $E$ and vanishes on an interval, so
$A_{0i}n_i=b_i n_i=0$; varying $n$ yields $A_{0i}=b_i=0$.

On the future null cone write $P=\rho(1,n)$ with $\rho>0$ and
$n\in S^2$. The identity becomes
$\rho^2A((1,n),(1,n))+\rho b(1,n)=0$ for every $\rho>0$; comparing the two
polynomial coefficients gives $A((1,n),(1,n))=b(1,n)=0$. Replacing $n$ by
$-n$ in the covector equation gives $b_0=0$ and $b_i n_i=0$ for every $n$,
so $b=0$.

The remaining massive-shell identity is
$A_{00}(M^2+r^2)+r^2 n^TA_{\rm sp}n+b_0\sqrt{M^2+r^2}=0$, where
$A_{\rm sp}=(A_{ij})$. Varying $n$ shows $n^TA_{\rm sp}n$ is a constant
$a$ on $S^2$. Taking $n=e_i$ gives $A_{ii}=a$; taking
$n=(e_i+e_j)/\sqrt2$ gives $A_{ij}=0$ for $i\ne j$. With
$z=\sqrt{M^2+r^2}$ the remaining identity is
$(A_{00}+a)z^2+b_0z-aM^2=0$ for every $z>M$. A polynomial vanishing on
an interval has all coefficients zero; since $M>0$, this yields
$a=A_{00}=b_0=0$, hence $A=b=0$.

In the quadratic null-cone equation, comparing $n$ and $-n$ gives
$A_{0i}=0$. Its value on $e_i$ yields $A_{ii}=-A_{00}$, and its value on
$(e_i+e_j)/\sqrt2$ yields $A_{ij}=0$ for $i\ne j$. Thus
$A=\operatorname{diag}(A_{00},-A_{00},-A_{00},-A_{00})=\lambda g$ with
$\lambda=-A_{00}$. This proves the null clause and completes the lemma.

Let $(M,g,N_0)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], let $x\in M$, and let
$M_*>0$ be a rest-energy parameter in joules. The **future massive shell at
$x$** is the Borel subset
$$\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}:=\{P\in T_xM:g_x(P,P)=-M_*^2,\ P\text{ future-directed}\}.$$
Use any smooth future orthonormal tetrad near $x$, whose existence is
[[thm-gr-local-lorentz-tetrad-existence]]. At $x$ write its basis as
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ and, for $q=(q_1,q_2,q_3)\in\mathbb R^3$ with energy
coordinates in joules, put
$$E(q):=\sqrt{M_*^2+|q|^2},\qquad P_e(q):=E(q)e_0+\sum_{i=1}^3q_i e_i.$$
Let $\lambda_3$ be Euclidean Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^3$
([[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]],
[[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]]). For every Borel set
$A\subseteq\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}$, with its subspace Borel sigma-algebra
([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]), define
$$\mu_{M_*,x,e}(A):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\mathbf1_A(P_e(q))\,\frac{1}{E(q)}\,d\lambda_3(q).$$
In these tetrad coordinates the shell equation is
$-(P^0)^2+|q|^2=-M_*^2$, and the future sheet has $P^0>0$, hence
$P^0=E(q)$. Thus $P_e$ is a bijection onto the shell with continuous inverse
$q_i=g(P,e_i)$, so it is a homeomorphism. Continuous preimages of Borel sets are Borel
([[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]]), and
$1/E(q)$ is a positive continuous density. The nonnegative Lebesgue integral
over a measurable set is [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]; the
positive-density measure theorem [[thm-indefinite-integral-of-a-nonnegative-function-is-a-measure]] makes
$\mu_{M_*,x,e}$ a positive Borel measure. Its coordinate expression is
$d^3q/E(q)$ and its units are $\mathrm{J^2}$.

Write $P(q)=(E(q),q)$ in the first tetrad and let $q'=Q(q)$ be the
spatial coordinates of the same future-shell vector in the second tetrad.
The tetrad change $\Lambda$ maps the entire future shell bijectively to itself;
the spatial coordinate and its inverse are smooth, so $Q$ is a global $C^1$
diffeomorphism of $\mathbb R^3$. Form the $4\times4$ matrix
$C(q)=[P(q),\partial_1P(q),\partial_2P(q),\partial_3P(q)]$. Block
elimination gives
$\det C(q)=E(q)-|q|^2/E(q)=M_*^2/E(q)$.

The chain rule on the shell gives
$\Lambda C(q)=C(q')\operatorname{diag}(1,DQ(q))$. Taking absolute
determinants and using [F2] and step 1.1 yields
$$\frac{M_*^2}{E(q)}=\frac{M_*^2}{E(q')}|\det DQ(q)|,\qquad |\det DQ(q)|=\frac{E(q')}{E(q)}.$$

For any Borel $A$ on the shell, apply [F3] to the nonnegative Borel
function $h(q')=\mathbf1_A(P_{e'}(q'))/E(q')$. Then
$$\mu_{M_*,x,e'}(A)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\mathbf1_A(P_e(q))}{E(q')}|\det DQ(q)|\,d^3q=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\mathbf1_A(P_e(q))}{E(q)}\,d^3q=\mu_{M_*,x,e}(A),$$
where the first equality uses the common geometric vector and the second uses
step 2.1. This is equality of positive Borel measures, completing the proof.

Let $(M,g,N_0)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], let $x\in M$, and let
$M_*>0$ be a rest-energy parameter in joules. The **future massive shell at
$x$** is the Borel subset
$$\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}:=\{P\in T_xM:g_x(P,P)=-M_*^2,\ P\text{ future-directed}\}.$$
Use any smooth future orthonormal tetrad near $x$, whose existence is
[[thm-gr-local-lorentz-tetrad-existence]]. At $x$ write its basis as
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ and, for $q=(q_1,q_2,q_3)\in\mathbb R^3$ with energy
coordinates in joules, put
$$E(q):=\sqrt{M_*^2+|q|^2},\qquad P_e(q):=E(q)e_0+\sum_{i=1}^3q_i e_i.$$
Let $\lambda_3$ be Euclidean Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^3$
([[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]],
[[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]]). For every Borel set
$A\subseteq\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}$, with its subspace Borel sigma-algebra
([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]), define
$$\mu_{M_*,x,e}(A):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\mathbf1_A(P_e(q))\,\frac{1}{E(q)}\,d\lambda_3(q).$$
In these tetrad coordinates the shell equation is
$-(P^0)^2+|q|^2=-M_*^2$, and the future sheet has $P^0>0$, hence
$P^0=E(q)$. Thus $P_e$ is a bijection onto the shell with continuous inverse
$q_i=g(P,e_i)$, so it is a homeomorphism. Continuous preimages of Borel sets are Borel
([[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]]), and
$1/E(q)$ is a positive continuous density. The nonnegative Lebesgue integral
over a measurable set is [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]; the
positive-density measure theorem [[thm-indefinite-integral-of-a-nonnegative-function-is-a-measure]] makes
$\mu_{M_*,x,e}$ a positive Borel measure. Its coordinate expression is
$d^3q/E(q)$ and its units are $\mathrm{J^2}$.

Let $x$ be an event of a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$M_*>0$, and let $e$ and $e'$ be any two smooth future orthonormal tetrads
near $x$. The measures $d\mu_{M_*,x,e}$ and $d\mu_{M_*,x,e'}$ defined in
[[def-tgr-future-mass-shell-measure]] agree on every Borel subset of the future
massive shell at $x$. Hence the fiber measure $d\mu_{M_*,x}$ is independent of
the chosen future orthonormal tetrad.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n \ge 1$,
let $S^{n-1} \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be the unit sphere, and let $\sigma$ be the
set function of [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]. Then $\sigma$
is a finite Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$, and for every Borel measurable
$f : \mathbb R^n \to [0,\infty]$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^n} f(x)\,d\lambda_n(x) = \int_0^\infty \int_{S^{n-1}} f(r\omega) r^{n-1}\,d\sigma(\omega)\,dr.$$
Moreover, $\sigma$ is the unique Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$ with this
property.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$S^2:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ and let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on $S^2$ of
[[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], a finite Borel measure ([[def-measure]],
[[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). Let

$$\Phi:(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)\to S^2,\qquad \Phi(\theta,\varphi):=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\ \sin\theta\sin\varphi,\ \cos\theta),$$

and let $H:=\{(x,y,0)\in\mathbb R^3:x\ge0\}$ denote the closed half-plane, a Lebesgue-null Borel set
([[thm-affine-hyperplanes-and-proper-subspaces-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]]). Then:

(a) for every Borel function $F:S^2\to[0,+\infty]$,
$$\int_{S^2}F\,d\sigma=\int_{(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)}F\bigl(\Phi(\theta,\varphi)\bigr)\,\sin\theta\ d(\theta,\varphi),$$
the right-hand integral being the Lebesgue integral over the open rectangle;

(b) $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$;

(c) the identity of (a) holds with $F\in L^1(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$ in the sense that $F\circ\Phi$ is Lebesgue
integrable on the rectangle against $\sin\theta\,d(\theta,\varphi)$ and the two integrals agree (real and
imaginary parts, positive and negative parts).

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

A **measure space** is a triple $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ in which $X$ is a set, $\mathcal A$ is a sigma-algebra on $X$, and $\mu$ is a measure on $(X,\mathcal A)$ ([[def-measure]]). The members of $\mathcal A$ are the **measurable sets** of the space.

Fix $n \ge 1$ and let $\lambda_n^*$ be the Lebesgue outer set function on $\mathbb{R}^n$
([[def-lebesgue-outer-measure]]). A set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is
**Lebesgue measurable** when

$$\lambda_n^*(A) \;=\; \lambda_n^*(A \cap E) \;+\; \lambda_n^*(A \setminus E) \qquad \text{for every } A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n .$$

This formula makes sense before any outer-measure theorem is invoked. Under
countable choice, [[thm-lebesgue-outer-measure-is-an-outer-measure-agreeing-with-volume]]
makes $\lambda_n^*$ an outer measure, and the displayed condition is then exactly
Carathéodory measurability in the sense of [[def-caratheodory-measurable-set]].

The family of Lebesgue measurable sets is written $\mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n)$,
and **Lebesgue measure** is the restriction

$$\lambda_n \;:=\; \lambda_n^*\!\restriction_{\mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n)} .$$

On the real line the subscript is dropped and $\lambda := \lambda_1$.

The quantifier over every test set $A$ is part of the condition, and no
hypothesis on $E$ is imposed before it is tested. That
$\mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is a sigma-algebra and that $\lambda_n$ is a complete
measure on it are not part of this definition: they are proved, under the Axiom
of Countable Choice, in [[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]], which is
recorded in this item's `justified_by` because it is a statement about the
objects introduced here. Until that theorem the symbols $\mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n)$
and $\lambda_n$ name a family of sets and a restricted set function, nothing more.

Let $n \ge 1$ and **assume the Axiom of Countable Choice**
([[def-countable-choice]]). Then

$$\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^n) \;\subseteq\; \mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n) :$$

every Borel subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]) is Lebesgue
measurable ([[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]]). In
particular every open set, every closed set and every countable intersection of
open sets is Lebesgue measurable.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. Let $f:X\to[0,+\infty]$ be measurable and define
$$\nu_f(A):=\int_A f\,d\mu \qquad (A\in\mathcal A).$$
Then $\nu_f$ is a measure on $(X,\mathcal A)$.

A **probability measure** on a measurable space $(X,\mathcal A)$ is a measure $\mathbb P$ with $\mathbb P(X)=1$ ([[def-measure]]). The triple $(X,\mathcal A,\mathbb P)$ is a **probability space** ([[def-measure-space]]); $X$ is its sample space and the members of $\mathcal A$ are its events.

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval and let $f:X\times I\to\mathbb C$
be such that:

1. for every $t\in I$, the function $x\mapsto f(x,t)$ is integrable;
2. for almost every $x$, the map $t\mapsto f(x,t)$ is differentiable on $I$;
3. for every $t\in I$, the function
   $$x\mapsto \frac{\partial f}{\partial t}(x,t),$$
   extended by zero where the derivative is undefined, is measurable;
4. there are a measurable null set $N$ and a nonnegative measurable function
   $g$ with
   $$\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$$
   and
   $$\left|\frac{\partial f}{\partial t}(x,t)\right|\le g(x)$$
   for every $t\in I$ and every $x\in X\setminus N$.

Then
$$F(t):=\int f(x,t)\,d\mu(x)$$
is differentiable on $I$, and
$$F'(t)=\int \frac{\partial f}{\partial t}(x,t)\,d\mu(x),$$
with the same zero extension in the last integral.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $n\ge2$, a bounded $C^1$ domain Omega and $F\in C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^n)$, $\int_\Omega\operatorname{div}F\,dx=\int_{\partial\Omega}F\cdot\nu\,dS$. Both integrals are finite, with the continuous interior derivative convention and the outward normal on every boundary component.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

For $x\in\mathbb R$, define
$$\sinh x:=\frac{\exp x-\exp(-x)}2,\qquad\cosh x:=\frac{\exp x+\exp(-x)}2,$$
$$\tanh x:=\frac{\sinh x}{\cosh x},\qquad\operatorname{sech}x:=\frac1{\cosh x}.$$
For $x\ne0$, define
$$\coth x:=\frac{\cosh x}{\sinh x},\qquad\operatorname{csch}x:=\frac1{\sinh x}.$$

The positivity of $\exp$ makes $\cosh x>0$ for every $x$. If $x\ne0$, then
$x\ne-x$, so strict increase of $\exp$ makes $\exp x\ne\exp(-x)$; hence
$\sinh x\ne0$. Thus all four quotients above are defined on exactly their
stated domains ([[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]],
[[thm-exponential-is-strictly-increasing]]).

For all real $x,y$,
$$\sinh(x+y)=\sinh x\cosh y+\cosh x\sinh y,\qquad\cosh(x+y)=\cosh x\cosh y+\sinh x\sinh y,$$
$$\cosh^2x-\sinh^2x=1,\qquad(\sinh x)'=\cosh x,\qquad(\cosh x)'=\sinh x.$$
Moreover $\sinh:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is odd, strictly increasing, and onto;
$\cosh:\mathbb R\to[1,\infty)$ is even and positive, and its restriction
to $[0,\infty)$ is strictly increasing and onto $[1,\infty)$; and
$\tanh:\mathbb R\to(-1,1)$ is strictly increasing and onto. On their declared domains,
$$(\tanh x)'=\operatorname{sech}^2x,\quad(\coth x)'=-\operatorname{csch}^2x,\quad(\operatorname{sech}x)'=-\operatorname{sech}x\tanh x,\quad(\operatorname{csch}x)'=-\operatorname{csch}x\coth x.$$

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

derivations.claim:
For $z>0$, the defining integrand of $K_j(z)$ is positive. Near $t=0$
it is bounded. For large $t$, $\cosh t\ge e^t/2$ and
$\cosh(jt)\le e^{jt}$; after $y=e^t$, the bound
$y^{j-1}e^{-zy/2}$ is integrable because $y^{j-1}\le e^{zy/4}$ for all
sufficiently large $y$. Hence each $K_j(z)$ is finite and positive. By
[F1]–[F2], writing $r=|q|$ and then $r=M_*\sinh t$ gives
$$I_{M_*}=4\pi M_*^2\int_0^\infty\sinh^2t\,e^{-z\cosh t}dt =2\pi M_*^2(K_2(z)-K_0(z)),\qquad z=\alpha M_*.$$
The endpoint terms in the integral of
$\frac{d}{dt}(\sinh t\,e^{-z\cosh t})$ vanish: the value is zero at $t=0$,
and its absolute value tends to zero at infinity since the exponential
$e^{-z\cosh t}$ dominates $\sinh t$. Thus
$K_2(z)-K_0(z)=2K_1(z)/z$, and
$I_{M_*}=4\pi M_*K_1(z)/\alpha$.

The same polar substitution in $Z_{M_*}$ gives
$$Z_{M_*}=4\pi M_*^3\int_0^\infty\sinh^2t\cosh t\,e^{-z\cosh t}dt =\pi M_*^3(K_3(z)-K_1(z)).$$
The endpoint terms in the integral of
$\frac{d}{dt}(\sinh(2t)e^{-z\cosh t})$ vanish by the same exponential bound.
Using $\cosh(2t)-1=2\sinh^2t$ and
$\cosh(3t)-\cosh t=4\sinh^2t\cosh t$ gives
$K_3(z)-K_1(z)=4K_2(z)/z$. Hence
$Z_{M_*}=4\pi M_*^2K_2(z)/\alpha$, which is finite and positive.

Interpret $d^3q$ as $d\lambda_3(q)$ on the measure space
$(\mathbb R^3,\mathcal L(\mathbb R^3),\lambda_3)$ of [F3]. The density
$Z_{M_*}^{-1}e^{-\alpha E(q)}$ is positive and Borel, hence
$\mathcal L(\mathbb R^3)$-measurable by [F3]. Thus $\nu_u$ is the measure
on $\mathcal L(\mathbb R^3)$ obtained by integrating this density against
$\lambda_3$; its total mass is $Z_{M_*}^{-1}Z_{M_*}=1$ by the definition
of $Z_{M_*}$, so it is a probability measure on
$(\mathbb R^3,\mathcal L(\mathbb R^3))$. Also $h_{\rm ref}^3c^3$ has units
$\mathrm{J^3m^3}$, so $n h_{\rm ref}^3c^3$ and $Z_{M_*}$ both have units
$\mathrm{J^3}$; hence $\zeta$ is dimensionless.

Differentiation under the integral sign in $Z_{M_*}(\alpha)$ is valid
near any $\alpha_0>0$: for $\alpha\ge\alpha_0/2$,
$E e^{-\alpha E}\le C e^{-\alpha_0E/4}$, where
$C=\sup_{E\ge M_*} E e^{-\alpha_0E/4}<\infty$ and the majorant is
integrable by $Z_{M_*}(\alpha_0/4)<\infty$. Thus
$-\partial_\alpha\log Z_{M_*}=\langle E\rangle$. For the defining $K_2$
integral, on $z\in[z_0/2,3z_0/2]$ the derivative integrand is bounded in
absolute value by $e^{3t}e^{-(z_0/4)e^t}$, an integrable function after
$y=e^t$. [F4] therefore permits differentiation and gives
$K_2'(z)=-\tfrac12(K_1(z)+K_3(z))$, since
$\cosh t\cosh(2t)=(\cosh(3t)+\cosh t)/2$. Combining this with the
recurrence in the preceding calculation gives
$K_2'(z)=-K_1(z)-2K_2(z)/z$. Differentiating the formula for $Z_{M_*}$ now
shows
$$\langle E\rangle=\frac3\alpha+M_*\frac{K_1(\alpha M_*)}{K_2(\alpha M_*)}.$$

The bound $|q_i|\le E$ and the finite integrals of
$e^{-\alpha E}$ and $E e^{-\alpha E}$ show that the current and stress
integrals are absolutely convergent: in the rest tetrad,
$|P^a|\le E$ and $|P^aP^b|/E\le E$. Their common prefactor is
$e^\zeta/(h_{\rm ref}^3c^3)=n/Z_{M_*}$. Oddness in each $q_i$ makes the
spatial current and off-diagonal stress entries zero; rotational invariance
makes the three diagonal spatial entries equal. The time component of the
current is $\frac n{Z_{M_*}}\int e^{-\alpha E}d^3q=n$, and the time-time
stress entry is $\frac n{Z_{M_*}}\int E e^{-\alpha E}d^3q
=n\langle E\rangle$.

On $B_R\subset\mathbb R^3$, apply [F5] to
$q\mapsto q e^{-\alpha E(q)}$. Its divergence is
$(3-\alpha|q|^2/E)e^{-\alpha E}$ and its outward flux is
$4\pi R^3e^{-\alpha E(R)}$, which tends to zero as $R\to\infty$ because
$E(R)\ge R$. The divergence is absolutely integrable since its magnitude is
at most $(3+\alpha E)e^{-\alpha E}$, whose integral is finite by the
partition and energy calculations above. Dominated convergence [F7] on the
increasing balls $B_m$ passes the bounded-ball identity to $\mathbb R^3$ and
gives
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{|q|^2}{E}e^{-\alpha E}d^3q =\frac3\alpha Z_{M_*}(\alpha).$$
The trace of the spatial stress is $n/Z_{M_*}$ times this integral, and its
three diagonal entries are equal by step 4.1; therefore each is
$p=n/\alpha$.

The shell measure is independent of the future tetrad by [F1], and the
integrals defining $J$ and $T$ are contractions of the geometric momentum
vector with that measure. Thus their rest-tetrad components from step 4.1 and
the pressure from step 5.1 determine the tensors intrinsically. In that tetrad
$J=(n,0,0,0)$ and $T^{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(\varepsilon,p,p,p)$. Since
$u=(1,0,0,0)$ and $g^{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ there, these are
exactly $J^a=nu^a$ and
$T^{ab}=(\varepsilon+p)u^au^b+pg^{ab}$.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $(M,g,N_0)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], let $x\in M$, and let
$M_*>0$ be a rest-energy parameter in joules. The **future massive shell at
$x$** is the Borel subset
$$\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}:=\{P\in T_xM:g_x(P,P)=-M_*^2,\ P\text{ future-directed}\}.$$
Use any smooth future orthonormal tetrad near $x$, whose existence is
[[thm-gr-local-lorentz-tetrad-existence]]. At $x$ write its basis as
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ and, for $q=(q_1,q_2,q_3)\in\mathbb R^3$ with energy
coordinates in joules, put
$$E(q):=\sqrt{M_*^2+|q|^2},\qquad P_e(q):=E(q)e_0+\sum_{i=1}^3q_i e_i.$$
Let $\lambda_3$ be Euclidean Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^3$
([[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]],
[[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]]). For every Borel set
$A\subseteq\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}$, with its subspace Borel sigma-algebra
([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]), define
$$\mu_{M_*,x,e}(A):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\mathbf1_A(P_e(q))\,\frac{1}{E(q)}\,d\lambda_3(q).$$
In these tetrad coordinates the shell equation is
$-(P^0)^2+|q|^2=-M_*^2$, and the future sheet has $P^0>0$, hence
$P^0=E(q)$. Thus $P_e$ is a bijection onto the shell with continuous inverse
$q_i=g(P,e_i)$, so it is a homeomorphism. Continuous preimages of Borel sets are Borel
([[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]]), and
$1/E(q)$ is a positive continuous density. The nonnegative Lebesgue integral
over a measurable set is [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]; the
positive-density measure theorem [[thm-indefinite-integral-of-a-nonnegative-function-is-a-measure]] makes
$\mu_{M_*,x,e}$ a positive Borel measure. Its coordinate expression is
$d^3q/E(q)$ and its units are $\mathrm{J^2}$.

Let $x$ be an event of a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$M_*>0$, and let $e$ and $e'$ be any two smooth future orthonormal tetrads
near $x$. The measures $d\mu_{M_*,x,e}$ and $d\mu_{M_*,x,e'}$ defined in
[[def-tgr-future-mass-shell-measure]] agree on every Borel subset of the future
massive shell at $x$. Hence the fiber measure $d\mu_{M_*,x}$ is independent of
the chosen future orthonormal tetrad.

Let $(V,g,C^+)$ be a four-dimensional time-oriented Lorentz vector space of
signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with future cone $C^+$ as in
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]. Let $M>0$ and let $A$ be a
symmetric bilinear form on $V$ and $b$ a covector. If
$$A(P,P)+b(P)=0\qquad\text{for every }P\in C^+\text{ with }g(P,P)=-M^2,$$
then $A=0$ and $b=0$. If instead this identity holds for every nonzero future
null vector $P\in\overline{C^+}$, then $b=0$ and $A=\lambda g$ for some
$\lambda\in\mathbb R$. The second clause is the exact massless conformal
exception.

Let $x$ be an event in a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$M_*>0$ be an energy in joules, and let $u\in T_xM$ be future unit timelike,
$g(u,u)=-1$. Fix $k_B>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, $T>0$ in kelvins,
$n>0$ in $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, $c>0$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and a reference
action $h_{\rm ref}>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Put
$$\alpha:=\frac1{k_BT},\qquad \beta:=\frac{u}{k_BT},\qquad E_u(P):=-g(P,u).$$
For $j=0,1,2,3$ and $z>0$ define
$$K_j(z):=\int_0^\infty e^{-z\cosh t}\cosh(jt)\,dt.$$
With the future-shell measure of [[def-tgr-future-mass-shell-measure]], define
$$I_{M_*}(\alpha):=\int_{\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}}e^{g(\beta,P)}\,d\mu_{M_*}(P),\qquad Z_{M_*}(\alpha):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-\alpha E(q)}\,d^3q,$$
where $E(q)=\sqrt{M_*^2+|q|^2}$ in a future orthonormal tetrad whose time
axis is $u$. Both integrals are finite and positive, and
$$I_{M_*}(\alpha)=\frac{4\pi M_*}{\alpha}K_1(\alpha M_*),\qquad Z_{M_*}(\alpha)=\frac{4\pi M_*^2}{\alpha}K_2(\alpha M_*).$$
The observer-rest momentum law
$$d\nu_u(q):=Z_{M_*}(\alpha)^{-1}e^{-\alpha E(q)}d^3q$$
is a probability measure. Define the dimensionless occupation and its number
current and stress moments by
$$\zeta:=\log\!\left(\frac{n h_{\rm ref}^3c^3}{Z_{M_*}(\alpha)}\right),\qquad f(P):=e^{\zeta+g(\beta,P)},$$
$$J^a:=(h_{\rm ref}^3c^3)^{-1}\int_{\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}}P^a f(P)\,d\mu_{M_*}(P),\qquad T^{ab}:=(h_{\rm ref}^3c^3)^{-1}\int_{\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}}P^aP^b f(P)\,d\mu_{M_*}(P).$$
These integrals converge, and, with
$$\varepsilon:=n\left(M_*\frac{K_1(\alpha M_*)}{K_2(\alpha M_*)}+\frac3\alpha\right),\qquad p:=\frac n\alpha=nk_BT,$$
they satisfy $J^a=nu^a$ and
$T^{ab}=(\varepsilon+p)u^au^b+pg^{ab}$. The quantities $J$ and $T$ have
units $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$ and $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, respectively. The reference
action $h_{\rm ref}$ is only a declared phase-space unit convention; it is
not Planck's constant or a measured parameter.

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ ([[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
([[def-derivative]]). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

$$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

Equivalently, since $b - a \ne 0$, there is $c \in (a,b)$ at which
$f'(c) = \bigl(f(b)-f(a)\bigr)/(b-a)$: the derivative somewhere inside equals
the average rate of change across the whole interval.

**Continuity on the closed interval cannot be dropped.** Differentiability at
every point of $(a,b)$ alone does not suffice: a function on $[0,1]$,
differentiable at every point of $(0,1)$ with derivative constantly $1$, for
which no $c$ works, is exhibited later on this page as a false statement, and
the companion page works the same witness out in full.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$S^2:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ and let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on $S^2$ of
[[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], a finite Borel measure ([[def-measure]],
[[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). Let

$$\Phi:(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)\to S^2,\qquad \Phi(\theta,\varphi):=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\ \sin\theta\sin\varphi,\ \cos\theta),$$

and let $H:=\{(x,y,0)\in\mathbb R^3:x\ge0\}$ denote the closed half-plane, a Lebesgue-null Borel set
([[thm-affine-hyperplanes-and-proper-subspaces-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]]). Then:

(a) for every Borel function $F:S^2\to[0,+\infty]$,
$$\int_{S^2}F\,d\sigma=\int_{(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)}F\bigl(\Phi(\theta,\varphi)\bigr)\,\sin\theta\ d(\theta,\varphi),$$
the right-hand integral being the Lebesgue integral over the open rectangle;

(b) $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$;

(c) the identity of (a) holds with $F\in L^1(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$ in the sense that $F\circ\Phi$ is Lebesgue
integrable on the rectangle against $\sin\theta\,d(\theta,\varphi)$ and the two integrals agree (real and
imaginary parts, positive and negative parts).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Then there is an open
neighborhood $U\subseteq M$ of $p$ and a smooth future-directed tetrad field
$(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ on $U$
([[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]), i.e.
$g_q(E_A(q),E_B(q))=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$ for all $q\in U$ with
$E_0(q)$ future-directed for every $q\in U$.

Every symmetric bilinear form on a finite-dimensional real vector space is congruent to exactly one normal form

$$\operatorname{diag}(I_p,-I_q,0_r),\qquad p+q+r=\dim V.$$

Equivalently, the numbers of positive, negative, and zero diagonal entries are independent of the diagonalizing basis.

Let $(v_0,\ldots,v_{r-1})$ be a finite linearly independent list in a real or complex inner product space. There is an orthonormal list $(e_0,\ldots,e_{r-1})$ such that, for every $k\le r$,

$$\operatorname{span}(e_0,\ldots,e_{k-1})=\operatorname{span}(v_0,\ldots,v_{k-1}).$$

It is obtained recursively from

$$u_k=v_k-\sum_{j<k}\langle v_k,e_j\rangle e_j,\qquad e_k=\frac{u_k}{\lVert u_k\rVert}.$$

For $r=0$, both lists are empty.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), with associated quadratic form
$q(v)=\eta(v,v)$. A vector $v\in V$ is

- **timelike** when $q(v)<0$;
- **null**, or **lightlike**, when $v\neq 0$ and $q(v)=0$;
- **spacelike** when $q(v)>0$;
- **causal** when it is timelike or null.

The zero vector $0\in V$ satisfies $q(0)=0$ and is consequently **none** of
timelike, null or spacelike: the null case explicitly excludes it, and the
timelike and spacelike cases exclude it by $q(0)=0$ together with the strict
inequalities. The **causal character** of a nonzero vector $v$ is the sign of
the real number $q(v)$, and the three names are attached to the three signs as
above. When no confusion arises, the pairing $\eta$ itself is written
$\langle v,w\rangle:=\eta(v,w)$.

**Each nonzero vector has exactly one causal character.** For a nonzero
$v\in V$ the real number $q(v)$ satisfies exactly one of $q(v)<0$, $q(v)=0$,
$q(v)>0$ by trichotomy of the order on $\mathbb R$, so $v$ is timelike, null or
spacelike, and no two of the three alternatives can hold at once. The causal
vectors are therefore exactly the nonzero vectors that are timelike or null,
and the zero vector is causal in no sense introduced here.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), with causal terminology as in
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], and let

$$T:=\{v\in V:\eta(v,v)<0\}$$

be its **timelike set**. Components and closures refer to the topology obtained
by using any ordered basis to identify $V$ with Euclidean $\mathbb R^4$;
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], step 5.1, proves that the
resulting open sets are independent of the basis. By that lemma the
set $T$ has exactly two connected components, and each of them is nonempty,
open, convex and path-connected. A **time orientation** of $(V,\eta)$ is a
choice of one of these two components. Fixing such a choice, write $C^+$ for the
chosen component and

$$C^-:=T\setminus C^+$$

for the other component; thus $T=C^+\sqcup C^-$ is a disjoint union and
$C^+$, $C^-$ are exactly the two components supplied by the lemma. Relative to
this choice a vector $v\in V$ is

- **future timelike** when $v\in C^+$;
- **past timelike** when $v\in C^-$;
- **future null** when $v\neq 0$, $\eta(v,v)=0$ and $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C^+)$;
- **past null** when $v\neq 0$, $\eta(v,v)=0$ and $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C^-)$;
- **future causal** when it is future timelike or future null;
- **past causal** when it is past timelike or past null.

The sets $\operatorname{cl}(C^+)$ and $\operatorname{cl}(C^-)$ are the
**future closed cone** and the **past closed cone** of the time-oriented space
$(V,\eta,C^+)$. By [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] each of them
is a convex cone, their intersection is $\{0\}$, and a vector is causal exactly
when it is future causal or past causal, in which case exactly one of these two
alternatives holds: no nonzero vector is both future causal and past causal.
The timelike vectors are exactly the points of $T=C^+\cup C^-$, and
$0\notin T$ because $\eta(0,0)=0$; since a null vector is nonzero with
$\eta(v,v)=0$, no vector is both timelike and null, so the classes above are
mutually exclusive where the definitions say they are: no vector is both future
and past causal, and no timelike vector is null.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Write
$N_p^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,N_p)=0\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]) and let $T_p$ be the
timelike set, with components $C_p^+$ (the one containing $N_p$) and $C_p^-$,
and with future and past causality as fixed in
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]] and
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Then:

1. $N_p^{\perp}$ is a $3$-dimensional linear subspace of $T_pM$, and $g_p$ is
   positive definite on it; equivalently, every nonzero $v\in T_pM$ with
   $g_p(v,N_p)=0$ is spacelike.
2. $g_p(v,N_p)\neq0$ for every nonzero causal $v\in T_pM$.
3. $C_p^+=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\text{ and }g_p(v,N_p)<0\}$, and
   $C_p^-=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\text{ and }g_p(v,N_p)>0\}$.
4. A nonzero $v\in T_pM$ is causal and future-directed if and only if
   $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)$, and causal and past-directed if and only if
   $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C_p^-)$. Consequently
   $\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$ is exactly the set of
   future-directed causal vectors and $\operatorname{cl}(C_p^-)\setminus\{0\}$
   exactly the set of past-directed causal vectors,
   $\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\cap\operatorname{cl}(C_p^-)=\{0\}$, and every
   nonzero causal vector is exactly one of future-directed and past-directed.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\xi$ be a smooth vector field
on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **Lie
derivative of the metric along $\xi$**, written $\mathcal L_\xi g$, is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field obtained by the flow definition of
[[def-lie-derivative-of-a-tensor-field]] applied to $g$: for the local flow
$\Phi_t$ of $\xi$,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g:=\frac{d}{dt}\Big|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*g .$$

The field $\xi$ is a **Killing field** of $(M,g)$ (an **isometry generator**,
or a **Killing vector**) when

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0 .$$

The equivalent local characterization

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0,$$

where $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and
$\xi_b:=g_{bc}\xi^c$ is the lowered field, is proved in
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]] clause (a); the definition
itself asserts neither direction. Whether a given metric has Killing fields is
a property of that metric: neither existence nor uniqueness of a Killing field
is asserted here, and a general metric has none beyond the trivial field
$\xi=0$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]).

**(a) Characterization of Killing fields.** For every smooth vector field
$\xi$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]), with
$\xi_b=g_{bc}\xi^c$ the lowered field,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0 .$$

**(b) Contraction along geodesics.** If $\xi$ is a Killing field and
$\gamma:I\to M$ is a geodesic with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its affine parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]), then $t\mapsto
g_{\gamma(t)}(\xi_{\gamma(t)},\gamma'(t))$ is constant on $I$.

**(c) Conserved current.** Let $U\subseteq M$ be open, let $T$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$, and let $\xi$ be a Killing field on $U$. Then
$J^{a}:=T^{ab}\xi_b$ is a smooth vector field on $U$ with
$\nabla_aJ^a=0$; consequently the flux balance of
[[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]] clause (b) applies to $J$
on every smooth singular $4$-chain contained in $U$.

**(d) On-shell conservation of the Hilbert tensor.** Let $c>0$, let
$S:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be a model action with Hilbert stress-energy tensor
$T$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to $c$
([[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]). For the flow diffeomorphisms $F$
below, suppose the configuration set $\mathcal X$ carries specified maps
$P_F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X$ with $P_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$; write
$F^*\varphi:=P_F(\varphi)$. For geometric matter fields these are the
model's pullbacks; no pullback operation on an arbitrary set is implicit.
For **every** smooth compactly supported vector field $\xi$, its flow
$\Phi_v$ is global
([[def-complete-vector-field]], [[def-local-and-global-flow]]); this holds for
every compactly supported smooth field, using the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] through
[[thm-compactly-supported-vector-fields-are-complete]]. Write
$G(u,v):=S(\Phi_v^*g,\Phi_u^*\varphi)$ for the simultaneous pullback by the
flow (this presupposes that the pairs lie in $\mathcal D$, which is part of the
hypotheses below). Suppose (H1)–(H4) hold for **every** such $\xi$ (with
its own $G$ and parameter neighborhood):

- **(H1)** the map $G$ is defined on a neighborhood of $(0,0)$ in
  $\mathbb R^2$ and is differentiable at $(0,0)$;
- **(H2)** $\partial_uG(0,0)=0$ (the matter configuration $\varphi$ satisfies
  its model equations in this direction);
- **(H3)** $\partial_vG(0,0)=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_MT_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g$,
  where $q^{ab}:=\partial_v(\Phi_v^*g)^{ab}|_{v=0}$ (the metric variation is
  represented by the Hilbert tensor);
- **(H4)** $G(s,s)=S(g,\varphi)$ whenever $(s,s)$ lies in that neighborhood
  (invariance of the action under simultaneous pullback by the flow).

Then $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $M$.

derivations.claim:
In coordinates put $G(x,P):=g_{ab}(x)P^aP^b$. Metric compatibility gives
$\partial_cg_{ab}=\Gamma^d{}_{ca}g_{db}+\Gamma^d{}_{cb}g_{ad}$, while
$$\mathcal L G=P^c\partial_cg_{ab}P^aP^b-2\Gamma^a{}_{bc}P^bP^c g_{ad}P^d.$$
After substituting the metric-compatibility identity, each of its two terms
matches one of the two connection contributions, by symmetry of the lower
Christoffel indices and renaming dummy indices. Hence $\mathcal L G=0$.
Therefore the geodesic spray is tangent to the total mass-shell level set over
$O$. Along any local integral curve $(x(s),P(s))$ in that level set, the
function $s\mapsto g_{x(s)}(P(s),N(x(s)))$ is continuous and never zero,
where $N$ is the time-orienting future timelike field. Its negative sign at
the initial point therefore persists, so the local flow preserves the future
sheet ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]). Thus $\mathcal L$ is
tangent to $\mathscr H^+_{M_*,O}$, although its base component generally
carries a point from one fiber to another.

If $\beta_x$ is future timelike, put
$\alpha=\sqrt{-g(\beta_x,\beta_x)}>0$, $u=\beta_x/\alpha$ and
$T=1/(k_B\alpha)$. Then $g(u,u)=-1$ and $\beta_x=u/(k_BT)$. In the
$u$-rest tetrad, $g(\beta_x,P)=-\alpha E(q)$, so [F2] and [F4] give
$$I_{M_*}(\beta_x)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-\alpha E(q)}\frac{d^3q}{E(q)} =\frac{4\pi M_*K_1(\alpha M_*)}{\alpha}<\infty.$$

The other nonzero causal and spacelike types have these orthonormal normal
forms. For a timelike vector choose $e_0$ to be the future unit vector in its
direction or its negative, according to its time orientation. Its orthogonal
complement is positive definite by [F7]; applying Gram–Schmidt to a basis of
that complement gives $e_1,e_2,e_3$. For a spacelike vector set
$e_3=\beta_x/\sqrt{g(\beta_x,\beta_x)}$. Its orthogonal complement has
inertia $(1,2)$ by [F7], so choose a unit timelike vector there and choose its
sign to be future. The remaining orthogonal two-plane is positive definite,
and Gram–Schmidt gives $e_1,e_2$. For a nonzero null vector start with a
future tetrad and write $\beta_x=\beta^0e_0+v$ with $v\perp e_0$. Nullity
gives $|v|=|\beta^0|>0$. Set $e_3=v/|v|$ and use Gram–Schmidt in the
positive two-plane orthogonal to both $e_0$ and $e_3$ to choose $e_1,e_2$.
Thus the normal forms are spacelike $(0,0,0,b)$, past timelike
$(-\alpha,0,0,0)$, past null $(-a,0,0,a)$, and future null
$(a,0,0,a)$, with positive parameters.

When $\beta=u/(k_BT)$, it is future timelike. The value of $\zeta$ in
the Statement gives
$e^\zeta Z_{M_*}/(h_{\rm ref}^3c^3)=n$. The complete moment calculation
in [F4] therefore gives $J^a=nu^a$ and
$T^{ab}=(\varepsilon+p)u^au^b+pg^{ab}$ with the displayed $\varepsilon$
and $p$. This is a normalization of the specified mathematical ansatz.

Since $f>0$, differentiating its logarithm along the geodesic spray gives
$$\frac{\mathcal L f}{f}=\mathcal L\log f =P^a\nabla_a\zeta+P^aP^b\nabla_a\beta_b =P^a\nabla_a\zeta+P^aP^b\nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)}.$$
The last equality holds because $P^aP^b$ is symmetric; the covariant
expression follows by differentiating $g(\beta,P)$ along a geodesic, where
$P$ is parallel.

For spacelike $\beta_x=(0,0,0,b)$, $b>0$, let $\theta_0\in(0,\pi)$ be
the unique angle with $\cos\theta_0=1/2$. By [F6] the cap $n_3\ge1/2$
has area
$\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{\theta_0}\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\varphi
=2\pi(1-\cos\theta_0)=\pi$. On it
$g(\beta_x,P)=brn_3\ge br/2$. For $r\ge M_*$,
$E\le\sqrt2r$, so the shell integral dominates a positive multiple of
$\int r e^{br/2}dr=\infty$. For past timelike
$\beta_x=(-\alpha,0,0,0)$, the exponent is $\alpha E\ge\alpha r$ and the
full-sphere radial measure is $4\pi r^2/E\ge c r$ for all sufficiently
large $r$, so its integral diverges. For past null
$\beta_x=(-a,0,0,a)$, the same cap gives
$g(\beta_x,P)=a(E+rn_3)\ge ar/2$, again forcing divergence.

For future null $\beta_x=(a,0,0,a)$, $a>0$, set
$\delta=M_*/r\in(0,1/2]$ for $r\ge2M_*$. Let $\theta_0\in(0,\pi)$ be
the unique angle with $\cos\theta_0=1-\delta$. By [F6] the cap
$n_3\ge1-M_*/r$ has area
$\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{\theta_0}\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\varphi
