Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let $R$ be
the curvature operator of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
with components $R^a{}_{bcd}$ in a chart.

**(a) Tensoriality.** For all smooth functions $f$ on $M$ and smooth vector
fields $X,Y,Z$ on a common domain, $R(X,Y)Z=-R(Y,X)Z$ and
$$R(fX,Y)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,fY)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,Y)(fZ)=fR(X,Y)Z .$$
Consequently, for every $p\in M$, the value $R(X,Y)Z|_p$ depends only on
$X_p,Y_p,Z_p$, and $R$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(1,3)$ on $M$ whose
components in every smooth chart are the functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] clause (b).

**(b) Coordinate formula.** In every smooth chart $(U,x)$ with Christoffel
symbols $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of $\nabla$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]),
$$R^a{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma^a{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^a{}_{cb} +\sum_e\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{ce}\Gamma^e{}_{db}-\Gamma^a{}_{de}\Gamma^e{}_{cb}\bigr)$$
on $U$, for all $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.

**(c) Point-normal formula.** If the chart is point-normal at $p$, that is
$g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}$, $\partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0$ and $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0$
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]), then, writing
$g_{ad,bc}:=\partial_b\partial_cg_{ad}$,
$$R_{abcd}(p)=\tfrac12\bigl(g_{ad,bc}+g_{bc,ad}-g_{bd,ac}-g_{ac,bd}\bigr)(p) .$$
Equivalently, $R^a{}_{bcd}(p)=\tfrac12\,g^{ae}(p)\bigl(\partial_b\partial_cg_{ed}
+\partial_e\partial_dg_{bc}-\partial_e\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_b\partial_dg_{ec}\bigr)(p)$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. Tensoriality of $R$ is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a).
Lowering its output slot with the smooth metric and contracting with the
smooth inverse metric are intrinsic tensor operations
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] clauses (b)-(c),
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]]). Thus these formulas give smooth
fields of types $(0,4)$, $(0,2)$, $(0,0)$ and $(0,2)$, respectively,
independent of the chart. Symmetry of $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $G$ is proved
separately in [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clause (d).

Let $(M,g,N_0)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], let $O\subseteq M$ be open, and let
$\xi$ be a smooth nowhere-zero vector field on $O$ satisfying
$\nabla_{(a}\xi_{b)}=0$ for the unique metric-selected connection $\nabla$
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Its local flow
$\Phi_s$ exists on the open flow
domains supplied by [[thm-flow-box-theorem]]. On every common flow domain,
$\Phi_s$ is a local isometry and preserves $\nabla$ and $\xi$. Consequently
it preserves the curvature tensor $R$ of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]], all finite covariant
derivatives of $R$ and $\xi$, and every tensor or scalar obtained from these
fields by finitely many tensor products, contractions, and smooth scalar
operations. The assertion is local; it assumes no complete flow or global
isometry group. It makes no claim about arbitrary quantum observables or their
analytic representation by local curvature data.

Let $O$ be a connected open subset of a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Let $M_*>0$ be a
rest-energy, let $\beta$ be a smooth vector field with units
$\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, let $\zeta:O\to\mathbb R$ be smooth and dimensionless.
For each $x\in O$, let $\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}$ be the future fiber shell of
[[def-tgr-future-mass-shell-measure]], and define the total future massive
shell over $O$ by
$$\mathscr H^+_{M_*,O}:=\{(x,P)\in TM:x\in O,\ g_x(P,P)=-M_*^2,\ P\text{ future-directed}\}=\bigcup_{x\in O}\{x\}\times\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}.$$
Define on this total shell
$$f(x,P):=\exp\bigl(\zeta(x)+g_x(\beta(x),P)\bigr),$$
and let $\mathcal L$ be the geodesic Liouville vector field on $TM$; in
induced tangent-bundle coordinates $(x^a,P^a)$ it is
$$\mathcal L:=P^a\frac{\partial}{\partial x^a}-\Gamma^a{}_{bc}P^bP^c\frac{\partial}{\partial P^a}.$$
The geodesic Liouville vector field $\mathcal L$ is tangent to
$\mathscr H^+_{M_*,O}$, and
$$\mathcal Lf=0\text{ at every }(x,P)\in\mathscr H^+_{M_*,O} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)}=0\text{ and }d\zeta=0\text{ on }O,$$
where $\nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)}=0$ is the covariant Killing condition
([[def-gr-killing-field]], [[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]]).
Since $O$ is connected, $d\zeta=0$ means $\zeta$ is constant on $O$.

For any vector $\beta_x\in T_xM$ with units $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, define its
shell normalizer by
$$I_{M_*}(\beta_x):=\int_{\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}}e^{g_x(\beta_x,P)}\,d\mu_{M_*,x}(P).$$
This integral is finite exactly when $\beta_x$ is future timelike. If so, with
$\alpha:=\sqrt{-g_x(\beta_x,\beta_x)}>0$, it equals
$4\pi M_*K_1(\alpha M_*)/\alpha$ as in
[[thm-tgr-juttner-partition-and-moments]]. In particular, for carrier data
$\beta=u/(k_BT)$, the choice
$$\zeta=\log\!\left(\frac{n h_{\rm ref}^3c^3}{Z_{M_*}(1/(k_BT))}\right)$$
normalizes the proper number density to $n$ and gives exactly the number
current and stress moments of
[[thm-tgr-juttner-partition-and-moments]]. This is a mathematical theorem about
the specified exponential ansatz; it does not assert that a material
thermalizes or that a physical equilibrium state exists.

Let $(V,g,C^+)$ be a four-dimensional time-oriented Lorentz vector space of
signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with future cone $C^+$ as in
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]. Let $M>0$ and let $A$ be a
symmetric bilinear form on $V$ and $b$ a covector. If
$$A(P,P)+b(P)=0\qquad\text{for every }P\in C^+\text{ with }g(P,P)=-M^2,$$
then $A=0$ and $b=0$. If instead this identity holds for every nonzero future
null vector $P\in\overline{C^+}$, then $b=0$ and $A=\lambda g$ for some

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim:
Put $a=s/L_0$. The Christoffel formula in [F1] gives as the only nonzero
coefficients (up to symmetry of the lower indices)
$$\Gamma^s{}_{ij}=aa'\delta_{ij},\qquad \Gamma^i{}_{sj}=\Gamma^i{}_{js}=\frac{a'}a\delta^i_j.$$
With $a'=1/L_0$ and $a''=0$, the curvature formula in [F1] gives
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ss}=-3a''/a=0$ and
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=(aa''+2(a')^2)\delta_{ij}=2L_0^{-2}\delta_{ij}$.
Contracting with $g^{ss}=-1$ and $g^{ij}=a^{-2}\delta^{ij}$ yields
$S=6(a''/a+(a'/a)^2)=6/s^2$.

Suppose a timelike Killing field $X$ existed on a nonempty open
$U\subseteq O$. It is nowhere zero, so [F2] applies and gives $X(S)=0$.
Since $dS=-12s^{-3}ds$, this forces $X^s=0$ at every point of $U$.
Therefore $g(X,X)=a(s)^2\sum_i(X^i)^2\ge0$, contradicting timelikeness.
This proves (a), including every smaller open region.

Suppose a normalizable massive stationary exponential existed on a
nonempty open $U\subseteq O$. Choose any point of $U$ and a connected open
coordinate ball $V\subseteq U$ around it. Restricting the ansatz to $V$
preserves smoothness, stationarity, and the finite shell normalizer. The
theorem [F3] would then supply a future timelike Killing field on $V$, which
step 2.1 rules out. Thus no such massive state exists on $U$. This conclusion
concerns only that ansatz and exact stationarity.

Metric compatibility makes the geodesic spray tangent to the null shell,
since, with $G=g_{ab}P^aP^b$,
$\mathcal LG=P^c(\partial_cg_{ab})P^aP^b-2g_{ad}P^d\Gamma^a{}_{bc}P^bP^c=0$
by the metric-compatibility identity in [F5]. On $G=0$ away from $P=0$,
the fiber derivative $2g(P,\cdot)$ is nonzero, so this is a smooth level
hypersurface; its nonzero and future conditions are open within it.
Thus restriction of $\mathcal L$ to $\mathscr H^+_{0,O}$ is defined. For a
future null vector $P$, the null-shell Liouville derivative of
$f=e^{\zeta+g(\beta,P)}$ is
$$\frac{\mathcal L f}{f}=P^a\nabla_a\zeta+P^aP^b\nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)}.$$
By [F4], its vanishing on the full future null shell is equivalent to
$d\zeta=0$ and $\nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)}=\lambda g_{ab}$; conversely those
conditions make it zero because $g(P,P)=0$. The factor is smooth since
$\lambda=\tfrac14g^{ab}\nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)}$. For
$K:=(s/L_0)\partial_s$, direct differentiation gives
$(\mathcal L_Kg)_{ss}=-2/L_0$ and
$(\mathcal L_Kg)_{ij}=2a^2\delta_{ij}/L_0$, with mixed components zero;
hence $\mathcal L_Kg=2g/L_0$. Also $g(K,K)=-(s/L_0)^2<0$, and $K$ is
future-directed since $s>0$. Thus $\beta=bK$ is future timelike and
conformal Killing, with $\nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)}=(b/L_0)g_{ab}$; for constant
$\zeta$ its null-shell
Liouville derivative vanishes. This proves the explicitly constructed
massless conformal branch without asserting a massive Killing equilibrium.
